subject: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada.williams@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle

Team — looking for final sign-off today on the Console workflow for the route-level quantization toggle (RBAC, confirmation modal, and audit/change history visibility) so we can lock copy + backend contract for Beta.

Proposed UX/workflow (current build):
1) Route -> Settings -> “Inference Optimization” panel -> Quantization Profiles.
2) User selects:
   - “Default (no profile)” OR
   - a specific profile version (e.g., qpl://llama-3.1-70b-instruct/int8/v3)
3) We run compatibility check and show warnings inline (GPU SKU class / max context / deployment tier).
4) Save triggers confirmation modal:
   - shows: route name, current setting, new setting, and “expected impact” (if available)
   - required checkbox: “I understand output quality may change; evaluate and monitor before broad rollout.”
5) On Save:
   - write route setting
   - emit audit log event with diff
   - change history entry becomes visible immediately

RBAC proposal:
- Only users with existing “Routes: Write” permission (same as other route config) can change.
- Read-only users can view current profile ref and compatibility status, but cannot modify.

Audit/change history proposal:
- Event name: route.quantization_profile.updated
- Include actor, route_id, org_id, before/after profile_ref, and result (saved)
- Console Change History shows before/after and links to “Audit Logs” export view

Open items I need explicit approval on:
A) RBAC: keep it at Routes: Write, or introduce a more granular permission for this toggle?
B) Confirmation modal: do we require typed confirmation for Beta (e.g., type route name), or checkbox is sufficient?
C) Audit log visibility: ok to show the audit log link inline for any user who can view route settings, even if they can’t export?

If no objections by EOD, we’ll proceed with the above.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Console & Tooling
Redwood Inference


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada.williams@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 9:38 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle

A) RBAC
Routes: Write is acceptable for Beta provided we treat this as a route config change (which it is). I don’t think we should invent a new permission this late unless we’ve already got a pattern.

Two requirements:
1) The audit event MUST include the profile identifier/reference that was chosen (including version), and must include “disabled/default” explicitly.
2) Console needs to show “who changed it / when” in the same place as other route config diffs.

B) Confirmation
Checkbox is sufficient for Beta. For GA, we can revisit typed confirmation if we see repeated mistakes, but I’d rather not add friction now.

C) Audit visibility
Linking to the audit log view is fine. Export/download should remain permissioned (whatever we use today for audit export). If a user can’t export, they should still be able to see the change history entry on the route (actor + diff).

One nit: please ensure the modal + logs do not claim “expected cost reduction” unless we have data. “May reduce cost” is fine.

-Naomi


---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada.williams@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 10:04 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle

+1 on not creating new RBAC surface area for Beta.

Implementation-wise: please reuse the same authorization check as other route updates (routes.write / route_config:edit). That gives us consistent behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private control planes.

Audit event fields we’ll want for compliance export later:
- actor_user_id + actor_email
- source: console
- route_id, route_name (if available), org_id
- before.profile_ref, after.profile_ref
- before.enabled, after.enabled (if you represent “default” as null, still render “default” in the audit payload)

Also: ensure no prompt/response payload ever gets attached to these events.

Marcus Lin
Security Engineering


---

From: Jada Williams <jada.williams@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 10:27 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle

Works for me.

Two UI details to confirm:
1) Change History row should show a clean diff even if the backend stores “default” as null. I’ll map null -> “Default (no profile)”.
2) The confirmation modal should show the exact profile ref string (versioned) and not “Recommended” or “Latest”. Otherwise we’ll get complaints about “silent changes.”

If/when we add aliases later, we should treat them as explicit values and log them as such.

Jada


---

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jada Williams <jada.williams@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 11:12 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle

Confirming backend contract is aligned with this.

Console backend endpoints (behind feature flag quant_profile_route_toggle + allowlist):
- GET /console/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings
  returns current { profile_ref | default }, plus compatibility status + any warnings
- PUT /console/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings
  validates permission (routes.write), validates schema, runs compatibility check, writes route config

Behavior:
- If user tries to enable an incompatible profile: return 409 with a structured error and remediation text (e.g., “Profile requires H100-class GPU; current deployment uses L4”).
- If user sets a compatible profile: save succeeds; runtime still has safe fallback to baseline if something changes at serve time.

Audit:
- Emitting route.quantization_profile.updated with before/after and actor.
- We’ll include a “change_id” that Console can link to in Change History.

Re: Jada’s point: we’ll only accept explicit versioned profile refs for Beta/GA v1 (no “recommended/latest” alias).

Chloe Martin
Console Backend

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada.williams@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 12:03 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle

Release/rollout notes:
- Please keep behind feature flag + allowlist for Beta. We’ll roll to design partners only.
- Confirmation checkbox is fine; no typed confirm.
- Make sure the UI surfaces the kill-switch behavior clearly in troubleshooting copy (e.g., “If your org admin disables quantization profiles globally, this setting will be ignored.”) — even if that’s not user-configurable in Console yet.

Also: change history needs to render even if the API call was made outside Console (e.g., API/terraform). That’s mostly on event ingestion.

Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering / SRE

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada.williams@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 1:41 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Console workflow approval: route-level quantization toggle

Approved from Product.

Decisions (capturing so we don’t relitigate later):
- RBAC: Routes: Write for edit; everyone with route view can see current setting + change history.
- Confirmation: checkbox only.
- Values: explicit versioned profile refs only (no alias semantics) for v1.
- Audit: must capture actor + before/after with “Default (no profile)” rendered explicitly.

Dylan — please proceed and tag me on the final UX copy for the warning text.

Marissa Cole
Product Lead
Redwood Inference
